headline: Approved prior meeting minutes; discussed Healy Park invasive removal and possible Forestry Reserve Fund use for tree planting.
summary: Mark Feigl, of the Merrimack River Watershed Council, updated members on a long-term invasive plant cleanup at Healy Park. Councilor Brown suggested using the Forestry Reserve Fund for tree planting and will research how. A public comment period on the U.S. Forest Service's ten-year urban forestry plan is open until December 4th.
decisions: Approved the October 22, 2026 minutes as written, by unanimous voice vote.

decision_evidence.quote: Ms. Corell moved the approval of the October 22, 2026, minutes as written. Mr. Regan seconded the motion. The motion passed by unanimous voice vote.

Conservation Commission Tree Sub-Committee 1 
Meeting Minutes  2

Council Chambers 4

In Attendance:  7 
Subcommittee Members: Tom Daigle (Chair), Craig Tufts (Vice Chair), Elizabeth Corell, John Regan, Steve Winnett, Rick 8

Absent:  Ted Diers, Brooke Gauthier 10 
Guests: Liz McKinley, DNCR; Mark Feigl, Merrimack R iver Watershed Council 11 
Staff: Beth Fenstermacher, Director of Special Projects and Strategic Initiatives of Community Development 12 
Chair Daigle called the meeting to order at 8:03 A.M.   13 
1.  Adoption of October 22, 2026 Minutes 14 
Ms. Corell moved the approval of the October 22, 2026, minutes as written. Mr. Regan seconded the motion. The motion 15 
passed by unanimous voice vote.  16 
2.  Committee Procedures  17 
Chair Daigle stated that this will be an ongoing item to insure the subcommittee is meeting City requirements and RSA 18 
91-A regulations. 19 
3.  Bob Pollock Tree Tour Policy 20 
Chair Daigle suggested that this item be called a “partnership” instead of a “policy”. Mr. Regan is working with Mr. 21 
Pollock to find a meeting date.  Topics for the meeting will include requested stipend, number of tours/year, 22 
introductions with Ms. Gauthier and Mr. Winnett who would like to use Bob’s research to host future tours.  23 
4.  Follow ups 24 
a.  October 24 th  Ethan Tapper Event 25 
Members that attended the event reported that it was excellent, and well attended.  Subcommittee members 26 
praised Ms. Russavage (not present) for pulling the event together.  Mr. Winnett reported the information learned 27 
about Mr. Tapper’s recommendations for invasive removal/control, including the use of the “Buckthorn Blaster”. 28 
b.  Invasive Species – education and outreach 29 
Mark Feigl from the Merrimack River Watershed Council (MRWC) was invited to provide an update on his work 30 
with invasives removal projects.  Mr. Feigl reported that he is working on a longterm clean-up project at Healy 31 
Park, and that David Gill (Parks & Recreation Director) has given him full license to do what he wants on the site. 32 
Mr. Feigl recently met on-site with Doug Cygan, the State’s Invasive Species Program Coordinator. Mr. Feigl 33 
discussed opportunities for future collaboration for the continued invasives management, and discussed creating a 34 
Friends of Healy Park, or some other “adopt a park” collaboration.  Mr. Feigl presented several ideas about 35 
redeveloping the park for recreation, including a parking lot, boat ramp, bike park, etc.  Councilor Brown shared 36 
contact information with Mr. Feigl and requested that they meet on-site to discuss his recommendations.   37

Regarding collaborations for other volunteer projects in the City, Mr. Feigl mentioned that he has a trailer of tools 1 
he can bring; however, he only works 8 hours a week and cannot commit to help organizing events. The 2 
subcommittee thanked Mr. Feigl for his time, and look forward to continued discussions for collaboration. 3 
c.  Opportunities to collaborate 4 
Chair Daigle will be attending an upcoming Chamber event with a goal to continue to grow the relationship with 5 
the Chamber.  6 
d.  Fundraising/Grant opportunities 7 
Ms. McKinley reported that press release for the 2027 Schoolyard Canopy Enhancement program will go out in 8 
January. She also reported that i-Tree is currently being sponsored by Davey Resource Group; however, it is hoped 9 
that the program will be re-funded through the government in the future. Mr. McKinley further suggested the 10 
subcommittee look at the recent tree planting partnership between Target and Arbor Day Foundation; Target 11 
employees planted trees in several cities across the US this year. 12 
Councilor Brown suggested that the Forestry Reserve Fund should be repurposed to fund the Sustainable Tree 13 
Program or other tree planting initiatives. Ms. Fenstermacher stated that the use of the Forestry Reserve is 14 
regulated by the RSAs and the City Ordinance establishing the fund. Councilor Brown will research how to use the 15 
forestry fund for tree planting. 16 
6.  New Business  17 
a.  Ms. McKinley reported that the public comment period for the U.S. Forest Service National Urban and Community 18 
Forestry Ten-Year Action Plan is open until December 4th. 19 
7.  Next Meeting Date 20 
Thursday, December 17, 2026 at 8 a.m. 21 
A motion to adjourn was made by Ms. Brown. The motion was seconded by Ms. Corell. The motion passed by unanimous 22 
voice vote.  23
